html:
The Paugussett are an Algonquian-speaking people of western Connecticut, along the lower Housatonic and Naugatuck rivers. Paugussett was also the name of their main settlement in the 1600s and 1700s. Some writers count them as a band of the Wappinger confederacy, and they were close to the Wangunk of the Connecticut River.

They fished, gathered shellfish on Long Island Sound and farmed maize. English settlers from the Connecticut Colony took most of their land in the 1600s. In 1659 a small reservation was set aside at Golden Hill, in today's Bridgeport, one of the oldest in the country. The Golden Hill Paugussett still hold a tiny piece of land in Trumbull, while their neighbours the Quinnipiac lost all of theirs.
